Date: 2027-04-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Exec roster priorities: Q3 offer staging & approvals

Team —

Attached is my suggested operational plan for the Q3 executive slate. High-level asks: please review priorities, proposed comp bands, and staging order so we can queue offers in a way that minimizes payroll overlap and maximizes hiring velocity.

Summary (attached: q3_exec_priorities.xlsx, comp_band_proposals.pdf):
- Role A: Head of Product — priority 1; candidate is at final loop, target start 07/05; recommended comp band midpoint + $10k sign-on.
- Role B: Head of Sales — priority 2; recruiting agency has shortlist; earliest start 08/01.
- Role C: VP Infrastructure — priority 3; long lead time for notice period (8–10 weeks).

Decisions we need this week:
1) Signoff on the +$10k exception for Head of Product (if approved, we will route offer immediately).
2) Confirmation of offer order (we recommend Product → Sales → Infra).
3) Any changes to comp bands or approvals required from the CEO/Finance.

Please reply with explicit OK/NO or comments by end of day Tue 2027-04-20 so we can lock docuSign envelopes and HR scheduling.

Attachments: q3_exec_priorities.xlsx (roles/timeline), comp_band_proposals.pdf (band table + rationale)

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-18T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec roster priorities: Q3 offer staging & approvals

Mina —

Thanks for the clear deck. A few operational notes inline:

- I support the Product role as priority 1. Candidate timeline looks tight; we should reserve a backfill window in the budget for potential overlap.
- Suggest swapping Head of Sales and VP Infra order: the Sales hire will ramp revenue faster and is pipeline-constrained; VP Infra candidate has a longer notice period, so staging later is acceptable.
- The +$10k for Head of Product is reasonable if tied to successful closure of final references and mutual acceptance.

On the comp bands: +10k will push the offer above our standard band cap by ~6%. If we go there, we should log the exception and have CEO sign-off.
